qa_pairs.scenario: A frequent traveler returning to Dhaka in June 2014 found themselves in a discussion with customs officials regarding updated baggage allowances. Confused by the recent shifts in policy, the passenger sought to understand the formal foundation of these changes. They wanted to identify the specific legislative power the government relied upon to amend the existing baggage rules for non-tourists.
qa_pairs.question: What legal authority was cited for the amendment of the Passenger (Non-Tourist) Baggage (Import) Rules, 2012 in 2014?
qa_pairs.answer: The amendment was made under Section 219(1) of the Customs Act, 1969, read in conjunction with Item 17 of the Third Schedule.

qa_pairs.scenario: An investor establishing a manufacturing plant within a new High-Tech Park in 2015 faced complex logistical hurdles regarding the movement of goods. To ensure their operations remained compliant with national standards, they needed to identify the exact regulatory instrument that defined the customs procedures for their specific industrial zone. They consulted the official gazette to find the order issued by the government in coordination with the National Board of Revenue.
qa_pairs.question: Which Statutory Regulatory Order established the customs procedures for industrial units in High-Tech Parks?
qa_pairs.answer: SRO 214-AIN/2015 established these procedures, issued by the Government in consultation with the National Board of Revenue.

qa_pairs.scenario: A long-time customs clearing and forwarding agent in Chittagong was reviewing their operational compliance as of mid-2016. Amidst a wave of administrative updates, they wanted to confirm the precise legal source that grants the National Board of Revenue the authority to set licensing rules for their profession. They needed to reference the specific section and schedule of the Customs Act that empowers these regulatory actions.
qa_pairs.question: Under which legal provisions does the National Board of Revenue derive its power to frame Customs Agent Licensing Rules?
qa_pairs.answer: The power is derived from Section 219(1) of the Customs Act, 1969, read in conjunction with Item 21 of the Third Schedule.

qa_pairs.scenario: A corporate tax consultant in 2022 was analyzing the complexities of integrating customs duties with broader VAT obligations. While examining SRO 23-AIN/2022, they noticed that the regulations were underpinned by multiple pieces of national legislation. They sought to clarify which specific act, operating in tandem with the Customs Act 1969, provided the necessary legal authority for these rules.
qa_pairs.question: Which law, alongside the Customs Act 1969, provided the authority for the rules enacted in SRO 23-AIN/2022?
qa_pairs.answer: The Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act, 2012, specifically Section 135, provided the legislative authority alongside the Customs Act.

qa_pairs.scenario: A legal researcher specializing in trade policy was conducting a deep dive into the regulatory framework for high-tech industrial zones in Bangladesh. While reviewing the 2015 order governing these zones, they noted that Section 219(1) of the Customs Act 1969 was the primary authority. However, they aimed to identify the additional specific sections of the same Act that were cited to support the customs operations in these zones.
qa_pairs.question: In addition to Section 219(1), what other sections of the Customs Act 1969 were cited in the 2015 order regarding High-Tech Park customs operations?
qa_pairs.answer: Section 13 and Chapter XI of the Customs Act 1969 were cited in conjunction with Section 219(1).

qa_pairs.scenario: A customs officer tasked with enforcing new regulations in early 2022 was reviewing the documentation for a recently published notification. The notification integrated various tax requirements, and the officer needed to be certain of its exact legal lineage to ensure proper implementation. They checked the text to determine which specific clause of the Customs Act 1969 was referenced alongside Section 219(1) to provide the legal basis for the rule.
qa_pairs.question: What specific clause of the Customs Act 1969 was referenced alongside Section 219(1) in the 2022 regulatory notification?
qa_pairs.answer: Section 21, clause (a) of the Customs Act 1969 was referenced.

qa_pairs.question: Which instrument was issued in 2014 to amend the Passenger (Non-Tourist) Baggage (Import) Rules, 2012?
qa_pairs.explanation: SRO 141-AIN/2014, dated 2014-06-02, specifically amended the Passenger (Non-Tourist) Baggage (Import) Rules, 2012.

qa_pairs.question: When were customs procedures for industrial units in High-Tech Parks first established via SRO 214-AIN/2015?
qa_pairs.explanation: SRO 214-AIN/2015 was issued on 2015-06-01 to establish customs procedures for High-Tech Park industrial units.

qa_pairs.question: Which instrument integrated Customs Act powers with the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act, 2012?
qa_pairs.explanation: SRO 23-AIN/2022, dated 2022-01-01, integrated Customs Act powers with the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act, 2012.

qa_pairs.question: What was the primary purpose of SRO 174-AIN/2016 issued on 2016-06-02?
options: To amend baggage rules for tourists
To establish High-Tech Park customs procedures
To enact general rule-making under Section 219(1) for customs agents
To integrate VAT with Customs Act
qa_pairs.answer: To enact general rule-making under Section 219(1) for customs agents
qa_pairs.explanation: SRO 174-AIN/2016, dated 2016-06-02, provided the enabling authority under Section 219(1) for the government to frame rules regarding customs agents.

qa_pairs.scenario: A customs officer is reviewing the legal basis for rule-making authority. They observe that in 2014, the National Board of Revenue relied on Section 219(1) of the Customs Act 1969 read with Item 17 of the Third Schedule to amend baggage rules. By 2022, when drafting new rules, the authority cited Section 219(1) of the Customs Act 1969 in conjunction with Section 21(a) of the Customs Act and Section 135 of the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act, 2012.
qa_pairs.question: How did the legal framework for the National Board of Revenue's rule-making power evolve between 2014 and 2022 regarding the scope of legislative integration?
qa_pairs.answer: The legal framework expanded from relying primarily on the Customs Act 1969 (specifically Section 219(1) and the Third Schedule) in 2014 to integrating powers from the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act, 2012 by 2022.
